en: Wren! There you are. Come round where I can see you. My ears are gone, child, but my eyes still work.
Last night the bell on the point went quiet. Folk in grey robes rowed off with it, singing.
I felt it through the floorboards.
The Drowned Choir, they call themselves.
Seven bells keep the Old One sleeping, and they mean to take every one.
You have the ear I lost. You'll hear where the bells are hidden. The first one sang out from the east.
Past the tidepools, into the Brinewood. There's an old ship rotting in the mangroves. Start there.
Keep your lamp lit, keeper. I'll keep mine.
East, past the tidepools, to the Rotting Hull. Go on now. The light will be here when you're back.
The Tide Hook! A barbed iron hook on a long chain, still cold from the sea.
Press U to throw it. It bites into iron rings and carries you across, and it drags crates and small creatures back to you.
You ring the Tidebell. The note rolls down through the wreck and out across the bay.
Far under the water, something vast breathes out, and sleeps a little deeper.
Empty slot. Pick a tool and press its slot key.
Move the cursor to look around
%s: blow the Wayshell and fly here
Press the new key or button. Esc cancels.
A barbed hook on a long line. Pulls small things in and Wren across gaps.
Heavy enough to crack boulders and flip armoured shells.
Moths that glow in the dark. Raise it to show what hides from light.
Catch the wind and glide from high places.
Looses arrows of frost that freeze water solid. It never runs out.
Swim deep water, and dive under it for a few breaths.
Its note shatters bone and shows the unseen.
Blow it outdoors and Mantle the sky-ray carries you to a woken Tidestone.
Dried puffers stuffed with blast-salt. Light, throw, step back.
A keeper's practice blade. Light and quick.
Forged in Cinderreach and quenched in the sea. Hits harder.
At full breath it sends a wave along its swing.
Stops small shots from the front while you walk.
Keeps the spray off. No protection to speak of.
Woven from shed scales. Hits hurt less.
Cut from the deep. Hits hurt far less.
Holds a potion or a sea sprite.
Holds a potion or a sea sprite.
Drink to refill every breath bubble.
If your last bubble pops, it breathes you back to life.
Each bell holds one phrase of the lullaby that keeps the Old One asleep.
Each one gives Wren another breath bubble.
The Saltmarrow light, small enough to carry. Keep it lit.
Shell coins. Saltmarrow's traders take them.
Points to the chests still shut.
Opens the way to this place's heart.
Opens one locked door in this place.
A Tidestone sleeps here. Touch it to wake it.
Tidestone. Mantle can't reach you in here.
Woken Tidestone. Find the Wayshell to fly between them.
Woken Tidestone. Mantle can fly you here.
How fast talk types itself out.
Doubles the size of messages and sound captions.
Show a caption for important sounds, like a hidden bell or an enemy winding up. An arrow points to sounds from one side.
Shifts colours so they stay apart for red, green or blue colour blindness.
How hard the screen shakes on big hits.
The tiny freeze when a hit lands.
Outline Wren and enemies, and put solid backings behind the HUD and captions.
Full white flashes, or soft ones that are gentler on the eyes.
Hold to hum, or tap once to start and again to stop.
Each kind of sound has its own volume.
Fill the screen, or play in a window.
More languages are on the way.
Change the key or button for every action.
Pick an action and press Interact, then the new key or button. The arrows and the left stick always move too.
Quit? Progress since the last Tidestone is lost
The game saves when you touch a Tidestone. Quitting keeps everything up to the last one you touched.
Copy it to which empty file?
Pick an empty file to copy into.
Wren lifts the lamp and flashes it once: I'll go.
Dunstan shoulders a coil of rope and wanders off towards the smokehouse, very slowly.
Saltmarrow. Mind the lamp, mind the tide.
You've been inside that old hull. I can smell the bilge on you from here.
Keep going down, child. Bells like the dark, and the Choir likes it better.
Morning, keeper. Sea's gone flat as a plate. No birds, no fish. Not a ripple.
Hessa's been up by the lighthouse since dawn, waving that lamp at nothing. Go and see her.
So the bell's gone. I felt the quiet in my nets before anyone said a word.
If you're heading east, mind the tidepools. The scuttlers there have got bold.
Mind the tidepools, keeper. Bold little things, those scuttlers.
The hull in the mangroves? My grandad swore she was a bell ship once.
Carried the bells out to their towers, he said. Then the sea took her crew and left the ship.
Wren! Wren! Old Hessa's been shouting for you all morning!
Well. Shouting. You know how she shouts. She's up by the lighthouse.
Are you going on an adventure? A real one? Past the tidepools?
Bring me something good. A heron feather. Or a crab with three claws.
You went in the Rotting Hull?! Was it full of ghosts?
Mum says it's full of ghosts. I said I'd go and check. She said no.
Keeper. Good. Do me a kindness?
My smokehouse rack's come down, and Dunstan's got the only good rope in Saltmarrow.
Dunstan's down by the barrels, most likely. Asleep on his feet.
He said yes? Without grumbling? Keeper, you've a gift.
Come by when you're back. There'll be smoked eel, and you'll be eating it.
Smoked eel when you're back. That's a promise.
Bell's quiet. Sea's quiet. Even the gulls are quiet. Whole coast's holding its breath.
Marga sent you? Was she asking nicely?
...Hm. Tell her she'll have it by supper.
The Stonebreaker Mallet! An iron-bound head on an ash handle, heavy enough to dent an anvil.
Press its item key (U or I) to bring it down in front of you. It bursts cracked boulders, drives pegs into the floor and flips armoured shells.
You ring the Ember Bell. A low, warm note fills the foundry, and the furnaces settle.
Somewhere under the bay, the great breathing slows. The fire is banked and low.
For a thousand years, seven bells have kept the Old One asleep beneath the bay.
At every turn of the tide a keeper rang them. Lately, only one keeper was left.
Last night, out on the point at Saltmarrow, the oldest bell went quiet.
You found it. I felt the Point Bell ring through the floorboards, clear as morning.
One bell home. Six more out there, and the Choir after every one of them.
Take this. The old keepers' Wayshell. Blow it under open sky, think of a Tidestone you've woken, and the sky-rays will carry you there.
Wren got the Wayshell. Outdoors, open the map and pick a woken Tidestone to travel there.
The next bell is crying out from the Kiln, in Cinderreach. Go on. I'll keep the lamp lit.
Cinderreach, child. Follow the smoke to the Kiln. The lamp stays lit.
You got the bell back?! Can I hold it? Just for a second?
...Fine. But I'm telling everyone I nearly did.
The Glowmoth Lantern! Pale moths stir inside the glass, and the dark around you thins.
Press its item key (U or I) to raise it, and again to lower it. Things that hide from the light can't hide from it.
You ring the Moth Bell. A soft, clear note, and every lamp in the mire flickers at once.
The wisps drift down and settle like snow. Far away, something huge turns over in its sleep, and lies still.
The Kite Cloak! Old sailcloth stitched over a frame of cane, with a red kite painted on its back.
Press its item key (U or I) to throw it open and glide. A fan's wind will carry you further. Press the key again to come down.
You ring the Storm Bell. Its note goes out over the crags, and the wind drops to a breath.
Clouds part over the bay. Deep below, the great sleeper stirs.
The Frostfang Bow! Pale ash wood, tipped with two fangs of ice that never melt.
Press its item key (U or I) to loose an arrow of frost. It freezes water solid where it lands, and never runs out.
You ring the Frost Bell. Its note rings clear under the ice, and the old glacier creaks and settles.
Far out in the bay, the frost on the water melts away. Down in the deep, the great sleeper stops shivering.
The Drowned Belfry: the Great Bell
The Diver's Helm! Old brass, a round glass window, and a smell of the sea that never quite leaves it.
Now you can swim deep water. Press its item key (U or I) while swimming to dive under for a few breaths, and attack to slash underwater.
You ring the Drowned Bell. Its note goes down and down through the green water, further than any bell should.
Far below, something vast turns over in its sleep, and settles. The tide along the Verge runs gentle again.

A crab with three claws, sidling about in the pools. Wren scoops it up.
Three claws! THREE! Wren, you're the best keeper there's ever been.
Here. I found it in the shallows. Mum says pearls like this hold a breath of the sea.
I named him Admiral. He pinches.
There's the keeper. Sit. Eat. No, the whole thing.
And take this jar. Every keeper needs one, for whatever the sea sends.
Rack's holding. Dunstan even helped tie it, if you can believe it.
The bell! Good. But from the gallery I saw something huge thrashing on the Wreck Strand.
Choir nets, I'd wager. On the strand, just this side of the Hull. Go and see, then come back to me.
Are you going up to see Hessa? Can I come? ...She'll say no. She always says no.
One day I'll have a lamp like yours. A real one, not paper.
Will you teach me the signals? I know some. One flash is yes. Two is no.
And the long one is... I always forget the long one.
Wren holds up the lamp in a long, steady glow.
I'm here! The long one means I'm here. I won't forget again.
Yes, no, I'm here. Yes, no, I'm here. I'm practising.
I saw you coming home with the bell! I flashed my lantern at you. Did you see?
Hessa gave you the old keepers' shell? Then you're a proper keeper now.
When you're old, I'll take over. That's the plan.
Felt that through the boards. It's dreaming, Wren. Of every one of them you sang quiet.
Go and keep it company a while. Mantle knows the way down.
Still dreaming down there. I feel every breath of it in the boards.
Pike's the name, Marlo Pike. If it's worth having in Saltmarrow, it crosses this counter first.
Glints only, mind. Shells and promises I can pick up off the beach for nothing.
Back again, young keeper? Go on, have a look.
You cracked that old hull open! The puffers are back in the shallows, fat as you like.
Dried, and stuffed with blast-salt. Keep them well away from that lamp of yours.
Pleasure doing business. Mind how you go.
Quiet tides now. Good for trade. Good for sleeping, too, I find.
A keeper's cap. Haven't seen one of those up the pass in years.
This is the Kiln. All seven bells were cast in there, from bronze and the Old One's shed scale.
The Choir came singing up the pass and took it. I'm the last founder, and I'm not leaving.
I'm not leaving, keeper. Someone has to remember how it's done.
You've been inside. Then you've felt it. They've stoked it white-hot.
They mean to melt the Ember Bell into something that wakes. Get it out of the crucible.
You pulled the Ember Bell out of my crucible. Not one founder before me managed that.
My forge is lit again. Here. Brinesteel, from the same metal as the bells.
It'll ring when it strikes true. Mind you listen for it.
The forge stays lit now. Come back if that blade ever dulls.
Put your backs into it. The bell's under her, and Vael wants it before the tide turns.
A keeper's child, all the way down here? Go home, little lamp. This is bigger than you.
She's waking! Leave the bar. Down the holes, both of you. Now!
Work those bellows! It has to run like water before the tide turns.
You again, little lamp? Too late. We'll pour it into a Waking Bell.
The slag's alive! Get back from the rim. Out, all of you!
Oh... look at them. Every light in the fen, dreaming the same shape.
That's a calf. The Old One isn't angry. It's grieving, and they're its dreams.
I sang them out of their lanterns for Vael. I won't do it again. Not for anyone.
The Marrow Tomb: Hall of Ribs
The Marrow Tomb: the Regent's Barrow
The Echo Horn! A curl of old bone bound in gold. Blow it, and the barrow answers.
Press its item key (U or I) to blow one long note. Bone that hears it shatters, and things that hide are shown.
You ring the Marrow Bell. Its note is soft, and it goes out over the dunes, over every bone lying in the sand.
Your kin are sleeping too. Far away under the bay, the great sleeper breathes out, slow and easy, the way the tide goes out.
So you carry Hessa's lamp now. I carried it once, before you were born.
I was her first apprentice. She taught me the lullaby, just as she's teaching you.
But I listened too closely. Under every phrase, the Old One is weeping.
Ring the bell, and listen. Then tell me we should keep singing it to sleep.
Many voices sing from the bay
A deep rumble from under the sea
You've met him, then. Vael. I felt the whole coast turn over in its sleep.
He was my apprentice. Best ear I ever trained. He said the Old One was weeping.
I couldn't hear it. My ears were already going. So I told him he was wrong.
And then I stopped listening to him at all. That's on me, not him.
Don't hate him, little lamp. He's wrong, but he isn't cruel.
Ottilie keeps the keepers' old training cave up in Frostspine. Go and see her.
Seven bells, and Hessa's lamp. You came all this way to sing it back under.
Listen to it, keeper. Then let the Choir finish its song.
...Wait. Your notes. All seven, in order. I never heard them like that.
It isn't weeping. It's dreaming badly, and nobody has sat with it.
I was right that it suffers. I was wrong about the cure. Go on. Its heart is waking.
Wren hums the last line: "Sleep, old heart, sleep."
Deep below, the Old One hums back. For the first time, it sleeps in peace.
So the Regent's gone to bones at last. Then you've earned this. Come, look.
Those bones out on the dunes were its family. It lay down beside them to grieve.
The Regent wanted a weapon. All it ever wanted was to sleep where they sleep.
Whatever that Choir hears weeping, child, it isn't anger. Go and ring your bell.
The Nacre Buckler! Mother-of-pearl, grown over a bell-ringer's shield in the dark.
The Abyssal Coat! Cut from something that lived far deeper than this. It is heavier than it looks.
The Tidecaller! A keeper's blade, lost in the Old One's mouth long ago. It hums with the tide.
It's asleep. Really asleep. I've never once heard it this quiet.
I'll stay. Someone should sit with it while it dreams. I'll know if it stirs.
Tell Hessa I'm listening now. She'll know what that means. Go home, keeper.
At dawn, Mantle came gliding down to the mouth of the Maw.
Wren rode home over a calm sea, with the sun coming up behind them.
Hessa knelt on the warm boards, laid her palm flat on them, and waited.
Far off under the bay, the Point Bell rang. She felt every note of it.
The boats went out on a gentle tide. The grey robes were folded away.
And far below, the Old One slept, and dreamed of nothing at all.
